refs.en: “Verily, His is the creation and the command.”
“He is the First and the Last.”

h3.use: Ask: “If soul and matter are eternal and uncaused like God, what makes God God?”

refs.en: “No bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another.”

h4.use: Ask just one question: “What deed earned the very first birth?”

refs.en: “O Bharata, whenever there is decline of righteousness and rise of unrighteousness, then I manifest Myself… to protect the good and destroy the wicked and to establish righteousness, I am born in every age.”

refs.ar: وَإِن مِّنْ أُمَّةٍ إِلَّا خَلَا فِيهَا نَذِيرٌ
refs.en: “There is no people to whom a warner has not been sent.”

h5.use: Start with Gita 4:7–8 (avatar in every age of decline) and present the Promised Messiah as the awaited reformer for all religions.

refs.en: Janam Sakhis report Baba Nanak praying five times and saying: “Curse on the heads of those who abandon prayer.”
refs.cite: Janam Sakhi (as quoted in the Pocket Book)

refs.en: The chola (cloak) of Baba Nanak preserved at Dera Baba Nanak carries Quranic verses, including Surah al-Ikhlas, Ayat al-Kursi and “la ilaha illallah Muhammadur rasulullah”.

sk1.use: With Sikhs, speak respectfully: mention the chola with Quranic verses and Baba Nanak’s Hajj.

refs.en: “The Guru to come will be a Muslim … with the qualities of the Shariah.”
refs.cite: Janam Sakhi (as quoted in the Pocket Book)

refs.en: “Nihkalank will be born at Sambhal… the avatar will come in the age (of darkness).”
refs.cite: Dasam Granth / Janam Sakhi (as quoted in the Pocket Book)

sk2.use: Ask: “Who is the awaited Nihkalank? A reformer near Batala fits the Janam Sakhi.”

refs.en: Baha’ullah warns his deniers not to treat him as earlier people treated the messengers “when the verses of God were sent down” — presenting himself as the sender of revelation.
“He will take to task whoever disbelieves in him, and punish those who deny what has appeared.”
“This day have I perfected your religion for you.”

bh1.use: Contrast: Baha’ullah abrogated the Shariah; the Promised Messiah served it. Read 5:4.

refs.ar: لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ
refs.en: “Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance to you under the tree.”

refs.ar: وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكُمْ وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ
refs.en: “Allah has promised those among you who believe and do good works that He will surely make them Successors in the earth.”

refs.ar: ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا
refs.en: “…the second of two when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion: Grieve not, Allah is with us.”

sh1.use: Read 48:19 and 9:40 — Allah’s pleasure with the companions under the tree, and Abu Bakr in the cave.

refs.ar: إِنَّهُ بَايَعَنِي الْقَوْمُ الَّذِينَ بَايَعُوا أَبَا بَكْرٍ وَعُمَرَ وَعُثْمَانَ عَلَى مَا بَايَعُوهُمْ عَلَيْهِ ... فَإِنِ اجْتَمَعُوا عَلَى رَجُلٍ وَسَمَّوْهُ إِمَامًا كَانَ ذَلِكَ لِلَّهِ رِضًا
refs.en: Ali: “The same people who pledged to Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman have pledged to me on the same terms… if they agree on a man and call him Imam, that is pleasing to Allah.”

refs.ar: لِلَّهِ بِلَادُ فُلَانٍ فَلَقَدْ قَوَّمَ الْأَوَدَ وَدَاوَى الْعَمَدَ
refs.en: “May Allah bless the land of so-and-so; he straightened the crooked and treated the ailing.”

sh2.use: Use Nahj al-Balagha letter 6 — a Shia source — where Ali accepts the earlier caliphs’ election.

refs.en: “We (prophets) are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.”

refs.ar: وَنَهَضَ نَحْوَ الشِّعْبِ مَعَهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ وَأَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ وَعُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ
refs.en: “He went towards the mountain pass, with him Ali b. Abi Talib, Abu Bakr b. Abi Quhafa and Umar b. al-Khattab.”

sh3.use: Take one objection at a time; for Ghadir ask: “If it was an appointment, why did Ali pledge to Abu Bakr?”

refs.en: The Prophet (sa): “I had permitted mut’ah for you, but Jibril came and told me it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection.”
refs.cite: Firdaws al-Akhbar (as quoted); see also Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Nikah

sh4.use: Point out Ali never practised taqiyya — he never hid his faith even in Makkah.

refs.en: Imam Husain held those who had invited him with letters from Kufa responsible for his killing.
refs.cite: Nasikh al-Tawarikh vol. 6; Jala’ al-‘Uyun vol. 2, ch. 5 (as quoted)

refs.en: Yazid, on hearing the news, struck his face and wept, saying, “What had I to do with killing Husain?”
refs.cite: Jala’ al-‘Uyun vol. 2, ch. 5, p. 528 (as quoted)

sh5.use: Use Shia histories (Jala’ al-‘Uyun) to show the Kufans who invited him betrayed him.

refs.cite: Al-Bukhari, Kitab-ul-Tafseer, Sura Maaida, Page 1411, Vol. 3
